name: Bari
title: UTM Hull Gauging in Bari | Ferries, Cruise & Grain Ships
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Bari for Balkan and Greek ferries, cruise ships and grain bulk carriers: car deck, ramp, hold and tank gauging.
h1: Bari Ship Inspection: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement at Berth
intro: Bari is the main Adriatic crossing point for the Balkans and Greece, with ferries to Croatia, Montenegro, Albania and Greece, plus cruise calls and a steady flow of grain and other bulk cargo. Owners of those ships ask for thickness readings between sailings, ahead of surveys, and before a sale. Atlantis NDT dispatches technicians from India to gauge decks, ramps, tanks and holds in Bari, without any resident staff, so each job is planned around the ship's timetable.

highlights.p: Ro-pax ships link Bari with the Balkan coast and Greece on regular rotations, so decks, ramps and ballast tanks can be gauged in short blocks across repeated turnarounds without cancelling a sailing.
Cruise ships alongside for a day provide a predictable window to check scrubber overboard lines and selected void spaces, supporting owners whose systems operate heavily across the Adriatic.

highlights.h: Grain and bulk at the commercial quays
highlights.p: Bulk carriers delivering cereals and other dry cargo can be gauged in holds and on hatch covers once discharge ends, a common request before special surveys or a change of employment.

port.h: The port of Bari: passenger terminals, commercial quays and the Adriatic trades
p: Bari is the capital of Puglia and sits on the central part of the Adriatic coast of southern Italy, directly across the water from the Balkan coast. The port is enclosed by long breakwaters that protect a harbour reaching from the old town to the commercial area to the north-west. Passenger and ferry terminals occupy the quays close to the city, cruise ships use berths in the same zone, and cargo operations are concentrated on the more industrial quays. Vessels approach from open Adriatic water, and the tidal range is small, so berthing depends on wind more than on water level.

Ferry traffic is what makes Bari distinctive. Ro-pax ships connect the port with Croatia, Montenegro, Albania and Greece, carrying trucks, cars and passengers on overnight or day crossings, and the timetable intensifies in summer when seasonal services start. Cruise ships arrive between spring and autumn and often turn around within the day. The commercial side of the port handles cereals, other dry bulk, containers in modest volumes, and general cargo, and liquid bulk is a smaller part of the picture than in the energy ports further down the coast.

These ships experience wear in predictable places. Ferry vehicle decks and ramps take the heaviest punishment from trailer traffic and road salt, and ballast tanks suffer from condensation and the thermal cycling of year-round service. Cruise ships tend to need attention on scrubber discharge piping and the shell near the outlets. Grain and bulk carriers show their age in hold frames and the underside of hatch covers. Because every segment is on a timetable, gauging has to fit short windows, and the best results come from a clear plan agreed with the superintendent in advance.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in Bari: passenger berths and commercial quays
p: Nearly all gauging in Bari is performed alongside. For ferries, the work is done at the passenger terminal berths during the hours between arrival and departure: vehicle decks are cleared, ramps are lowered and the team works along marked grids on the plating. Overnight services spend longer in port during the day, which provides more time, whereas fast daytime rotations allow only limited coverage per call. Cruise ships present similar constraints, with the added requirement that passenger and crew movements are kept away from the work area.

Commercial quays suit bulk and general cargo ships. After discharge, holds are cleaned and made safe for entry, and the team measures frames, bulkheads, tank tops and hatch covers. There is no large commercial drydock in Bari for big merchant ships, so owners usually arrange dockings at yards in Italy, Greece, Croatia or Malta, and a survey in Bari beforehand gives the yard a measured steel estimate. Ships waiting for a berth can anchor off the port, where an owner's condition check on accessible spaces is possible when the sea is calm.
list: Ferry terminal berths — vehicle deck, ramps and ballast tanks of ro-pax ships gauged during turnaround between crossings
Cruise berths — scrubber overboard piping, selected void spaces and ballast tanks gauged during a day call
Commercial quays — hold frames, tank tops, hatch covers and coamings on cereal and dry bulk carriers after discharge
Container and general cargo berths — hatch covers, cross-deck structure and tank readings on feeder and multipurpose ships
Anchorage off the port — owner's condition checks on ships waiting for a berth, arranged through the ship's agent

context.h: Port state control and regulation for Bari's ferry and bulk traffic
p: The Italian Coast Guard boards ships for port state control in Bari through the harbour master (Capitaneria di Porto), under the Paris MoU. Passenger ships and ro-pax ferries are covered by the EU's rules for passenger ship surveys, and the owners of older ferries on the Balkan routes face regular scrutiny of structural condition. Bulk carriers come under ESP requirements from their first renewal, and port state control inspectors look closely at hold frames, hatch covers and coamings. A recent set of measured readings can answer questions during a boarding that would otherwise need an unplanned survey.

Beyond inspections, commercial decisions bring up thickness records. Ferry owners deciding between a refit and a replacement need credible steel numbers, and the EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on ships calling at EU ports, which makes sale and disposal planning a documented process. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime add cost pressure on older ferries and bulkers. On the Albania and Montenegro routes, charterers and sale-and-purchase brokers often request gauging records before agreeing terms, and a report prepared in Bari gives them a firm basis.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Bari
jobs.p: Bari jobs divide between ferries on a timetable and bulk ships on a cargo calendar. For ferries we measure in blocks, completing a defined set of decks, ramps or tanks on each call, then compile the full result. For bulk carriers we plan the work around discharge and cleaning. In every case the list of spaces, permits and the report format are agreed with the superintendent before the technicians leave India.
list: Vehicle deck and bow and stern ramp gauging on a Balkan-service ro-pax ship, spread across several turnarounds before a renewal survey
Ballast tank readings on a ferry during an off-season lay-by, to help the repair yard plan steel renewal
Scrubber overboard piping and shell wall-thickness check on a cruise ship during a day call, repeated on later calls to trend loss
Hold frame and hatch cover gauging on a grain carrier after discharge at the commercial quays
Owner's condition survey of a container feeder at anchor off the port before a charter extension

logistics: Bari Karol Wojtyla Airport is a short road journey from the port and has good European connections, which makes it the usual entry point for our teams. The ship's agent arranges ISPS access for the passenger and commercial berths and books any launch needed for anchorage work. Our technicians are Indian nationals travelling on Schengen visas, so we begin the application once the call is confirmed and finalise flights when the ferry slot or the berth time is fixed. For repeat ferry work we plan visas around the rotation instead of one call.
vessels: Ro-pax ferries to Croatia, Montenegro, Albania and Greece

faqs.q: How much of a ferry can be gauged during one turnaround in Bari?
faqs.a: That depends on the timetable. A short daytime rotation allows a limited block, such as one vehicle deck or a ramp, while an overnight ship in port during the day allows much more. We agree the block in advance, mark the grid on the plating, and continue on the next call, then combine all readings in one report.

faqs.q: Can cruise ship scrubber piping be measured in a day call?
faqs.a: Yes, for accessible sections. The overboard line, the discharge valves and the shell near the outlet can be measured while the ship is alongside, provided the system is shut down and access is safe. Repeating the readings on later calls shows how fast the pipe wall is thinning.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Bari for merchant ships?
faqs.a: Not for large merchant ships on a regular basis. Owners usually book yards elsewhere in Italy, in Greece, in Croatia or in Malta. We can gauge the ship in Bari beforehand to give the yard measured estimates, and mobilise the same team to the yard for the full programme if you want continuity in the readings.

faqs.q: Can hold gauging be done on a grain carrier at the quay?
faqs.a: Yes, once the cargo is out, the hold is cleaned and a valid entry permit is issued. Residual grain dust and moisture affect readings, so we agree who prepares the locations. We measure frames, bulkheads and tank tops and record surface condition against every reading.

faqs.q: What if the ferry is delayed and misses its slot in Bari?
faqs.a: We adapt the scope. A late ferry has a shorter window, so we start with the highest-priority spaces, record what was completed and move the rest to the next call. Flights are fixed only when the slot is firm, which avoids wasted travel if the schedule changes.
